Access Control Listc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#AccessControlList

A structured list of access control entries (ACEs) that governs which principals (users, groups, or system accounts) are permitted or denied specific operations on a resource.
has super-classes
Digital Artifact c
is in domain of
grantedTo op, protects op

Accountc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Account

A named account held by an Agent with a provider — an authenticated-access identity, a value-holding ledger position, or both aspects together — identified by one or more Identifiers and optionally attributed to a known Agent.
has super-classes
Digital Identity c
has sub-classes
Financial Account c, User Account c
is in domain of
accountOf op
is in range of
hasAccount op

Account Typec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#AccountType

A classification of a user account by its authentication or deployment context.
has super-classes
Category c
is in range of
hasAccountType op
has members
Cloud ni, Domain ni, Local ni, Service ni

Actuatorc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Actuator

A physical device that effects a change in a physical process or plant — for example a valve, motor, relay, or servo — as distinct from a cyber security safeguard mechanism.
has super-classes
Physical Artifact c

Agentc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Agent

Any entity that can act, perform actions, or be attributed responsibility in a cyber or sociotechnical context.
has super-classes
Cyber Entity c
has sub-classes
AI Agent c, Digital Identity c, Group c, Organization c, Person c, Threat Actor c
is in domain of
compromisedIn op, hasAccount op, hasEmail op, hasPhoneNumber op, originatesFrom op, usesInfrastructure op, vendorOf op
is in range of
accountOf op, affiliatedWith op, attributedToAgent op, authoredBy op, conductedBy op, createdBy op, emailOf op, hasVendor op, hostedBy op, issuedBy op, issuedTo op, ownedBy op, performedBy op, phoneNumberOf op, registeredTo op, registeredWith op, reportedBy op, sightedBy op

BOM Entryc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#BomEntry

BomEntry is the STONEWORK representation of a CycloneDX component element or SPDX package entry. It links a VersionedProduct into the context of a particular SBOM document via stonework:installationOf, and may carry component-specific metadata (PURL, license, hash, component type) that does not belong on the VersionedProduct itself.
A single component entry within a Software Bill of Materials, asserting that a specific VersionedProduct is included in the artifact or system described by the SBOM.
has super-classes
Component Context c
is in range of
has BOM entry op

Campaignc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Campaign

has super-classes
Cyber Activity c
is in domain of
affectsAsset op, conductedBy op, investigatedBy op, objective dp, posesThreat op
is in range of
consistsOfCampaign op, investigates op, involvesCampaign op, observedIn op

Component Contextc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#ComponentContext

An abstract class representing a context-specific reference to a VersionedProduct: the same product version appears differently depending on whether it is declared in a bill of materials or observed as a running installation on a specific system.
has sub-classes
BOM Entry c, Product Installation c

Controlc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Control

Instances of stonework:Control may represent individual controls, control enhancements, or sub‑controls. Framework‑specific identifiers (e.g., "AC‑2", "CIS 4.1") SHOULD be modeled using explicit properties rather than encoded in the class IRI. Control text SHOULD be referenced via citations rather than reproduced verbatim.
A prescribed security or privacy safeguard that specifies an action, capability, or condition intended to reduce risk, enforce policy, or achieve a defined protection objective within an information system or organization.
has super-classes
Behavior c, Countermeasure c
is in domain of
appliesTo op, controlBaseline dp, controlFamily dp, controlId dp
is in range of
appliesControl op

has super-classes

is in range of

A running or terminated process instance on a host, identified by PID, executable path, command line, parent process, and associated user account.
has super-classes
Digital Artifact c
is in domain of
accessesFile op, accessesRegistry op, commandLine dp, createsMutex op, executablePath dp, executedOn op, hasParentProcess op, launchedBy op, parentPid dp, pid dp, spawns op
is in range of
hasParentProcess op, initiatedBy op, runs op, spawns op

Sectorc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Sector

A broad division or category of economic activity, infrastructure, or society used for classification and targeting purposes.
has super-classes
Category c
has sub-classes
Industry c
is in range of
operatesIn op

Security Actuationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#SecurityActuation

A specific cyber activity in which a deployed security mechanism changes the security state of one or more cyber entities.
has super-classes
Cyber Activity c
is in domain of
appliesCountermeasure op, madeByActuator op
is in range of
madeActuation op

Security Actuatorc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#SecurityActuator

A deployed system, service, appliance, or software agent capable of changing the security state of a cyber environment by applying a countermeasure.
has super-classes
Infrastructure c
is in domain of
implementsCountermeasure op, madeActuation op
is in range of
madeByActuator op

Security Conditionc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#SecurityCondition

A state, circumstance, or disposition relevant to the security posture of a system, asset, or mission — existing independently of any measurement or assessment.
has super-classes
Cyber Entity c
has sub-classes
Threat c, Vulnerability c, Weakness c
is in domain of
observedIn op

Security Observationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#SecurityObservation

A time-bounded record produced by a security sensor or automated tool capturing one or more cyber observables witnessed in a monitored environment, together with frequency metadata.
has super-classes
Intelligence Product c
is in domain of
hasObservable op, madeBySensor op

Sensorc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Sensor

A deployed system, appliance, agent, or network tap that collects data about digital artifacts, network activity, or adversary behavior for detection and investigation purposes.
has super-classes
Infrastructure c
is in domain of
usesRule op
is in range of
detectedBy op, generatedBy op, madeBySensor op

Sightingc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Sighting

Records that a object such as an indicator, malware, tool, or threat actor was seen. Wraps observation metadata around a reference to the sighted object.
has super-classes
Intelligence Product c
is in domain of
evidencedBy op, reportedBy op, sightedAt op, sightedBy op, sightedObject op, sightingCount dp

Signaturec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Signature

A content-centric detection rule that matches malicious activity by a specific pattern — a byte sequence, string, hash, regular expression, or network packet structure.
has super-classes
Detection Rule c
is in range of
hasSignature op

Software Bill of Materialsc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#SoftwareBillOfMaterials

An SBOM asserts that specific VersionedProduct instances are components of a containing artifact. Component entries are represented as stonework:BomEntry instances linked via stonework:hasBomEntry.
A formal, machine-readable inventory of VersionedProduct components that constitute a software artifact or system, expressed in a standard format such as CycloneDX or SPDX.
is in domain of
has BOM entry op

Sophistication Levelc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#SophisticationLevel

A classification of a threat actor's assessed technical sophistication.
has super-classes
Category c
is in range of
hasSophisticationLevel op
has members
Advanced ni, Expert ni, Innovator ni, Intermediate ni, Minimal ni, None ni, Strategic ni

Stepc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Step

A single, individually addressable unit of action within a Behavior that models a multi-step process, such as a Procedure, Playbook, ThreatScenario, or Control.
has super-classes
Behavior c
is in domain of
isStepOf op, precededByStep op, stepOrder dp, usesDetectionRule op
is in range of
correspondsToStep op, fromStep op, hasStep op, precededByStep op, toStep op

Tacticc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Tactic

Instances of stonework:Tactic SHOULD correspond to high‑level adversary goals. Techniques are typically modeled as children or members of a tactic.
A high‑level objective or strategic goal that groups related techniques by the purpose they serve during an operation.
has super-classes
Behavior c
has sub-classes
Defensive Tactic c, Laundering Stage c, Offensive Tactic c
is in domain of
hasTechnique op
is in range of
techniqueOf op

Techniquec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Technique

Mirrors D3FEND's Technique class and reflects the PROV-O Plan philosophy: a technique is a plan that describes how an action should be carried out, distinct from the activity that executes it. Subclassed by stonework:CyberTechnique for cyber-specific methods.
A reusable, prescribed method for achieving an objective, which may be instantiated as a concrete execution by an actor or system.
has super-classes
Behavior c
has sub-classes
AI Technique c, Analytic Technique c, Cyber Technique c, Illicit Finance Technique c
is in domain of
hasTechnique op, techniqueOf op
is in range of
employs op, hasTechnique op, implementsTechnique op, procedureFor op, techniqueOf op

Threatc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Threat

Instances of stonework:Threat may describe adversary capabilities, strategic objectives, targeting patterns, or environmental conditions that increase the likelihood of harmful action. Threats may be linked to threat actors, campaigns, malware, TTPs, weaknesses, or assets, but are conceptually distinct from the actions or events that realize them.
A potential or actual source of harm arising from an adversary's capability, intent, and opportunity to exploit weaknesses or create adverse effects within a system, organization, or mission.
has super-classes
Security Condition c
is in domain of
manifestsAs op
is in range of
posesThreat op

Threat Actorc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#ThreatActor

An entity that has the capability and intent to conduct harmful activities within a cyber or sociotechnical context.
has super-classes
Agent c
has sub-classes
Threat Actor Group c, Threat Actor Individual c
is in domain of
employs op, hasMember op, hasMotivation op, hasResourceLevel op, hasSophisticationLevel op, hasThreatActorType op, investigatedBy op, objective dp, operatesIn op, posesThreat op
is in range of
addresses op, investigates op, memberOf op, scenarioActor op

Threat Actor Groupc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#ThreatActorGroup

A collective, organization, or coordinated set of individuals operating with common intent to conduct adversarial cyber activities.
has super-classes
Threat Actor c

Threat Actor Individualc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#ThreatActorIndividual

A single, identifiable human actor with the capability and intent to conduct adversarial cyber activities.
has super-classes
Threat Actor c

Threat Actor Rolec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#ThreatActorRole

A controlled role type describing the function played by a threat actor within a specific operation, campaign, or criminal organization.
has super-classes
Category c, Role c
has members
Agent ni, Director ni, Infrastructure Architect ni, Infrastructure Operator ni, Malware Author ni, Sponsor ni

Threat Actor Typec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#ThreatActorType

A classification of a threat actor by their organizational form, affiliation, or primary mode of operation.
has super-classes
Category c
is in range of
hasThreatActorType op
has members
Activist ni, Competitor ni, Crime Syndicate ni, Criminal ni, Hacker ni, Insider Accidental ni, Insider Disgruntled ni, Nation State ni, Sensationalist ni, Spy ni, Terrorist ni

Threat Scenarioc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#ThreatScenario

A plan specification describing how a threat could materialize against specific assets or missions — incorporating adversary intent, capability, opportunity, preconditions, attack path, and expected consequences.
has super-classes
Behavior c
is in domain of
addresses op, scenarioActor op, scenarioAsset op, scenarioTechnique op
is in range of
manifestsAs op, riskOfScenario op

Toolc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Tool

Legitimate software that can be used offensively by threat actors or defensively by security practitioners. Distinguishable from malware by being designed for benign or dual-use purposes rather than being inherently malicious.
has super-classes
Product c
is in domain of
communicatesWith op, downloads op
is in range of
downloads op, employs op

Transaction Typec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#TransactionType

A classification of a financial transaction by the kind of movement it represents.
has super-classes
Category c
has members
Currency Exchange ni, Deposit ni, Fee ni, Payment ni, Transfer ni, Withdrawal ni

Transitionc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Transition

A directed edge between two Steps within the same parent Behavior's Step graph, representing progression from one Step to the next.
is in domain of
fromStep op, guardLiteralValue dp, guardOperator op, guardType op, guardVariable op, toStep op

URIc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#URI

Represents a Uniform Resource Identifier conforming to RFC 3986.
has super-classes
Identifier c
is in domain of
uriValue dp, urlOf op
is in range of
communicatesWith op

User Accountc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#UserAccount

An authenticated-access identity on a system or service — a local OS account, cloud or directory account, application account, or social media account — through which a principal logs in and acts.
has super-classes
Account c
is in domain of
accountName dp, controls op, hasAccountType op, isPrivileged dp, loggedInTo op
is in range of
grantedTo op, launchedBy op

User Agentc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#UserAgent

A string identifier transmitted by a client application in HTTP requests declaring the software, version, and platform making the request. Used for fingerprinting clients, identifying malware C2 beaconing patterns, and clustering infrastructure by shared tooling.
has super-classes
Identifier c
is in domain of
userAgentString dp

User Groupc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#UserGroup

Represents a user group on a system or service, including local OS groups, cloud groups, and social media groups.
has super-classes
Digital Identity c
is in domain of
groupName dp
is in range of
grantedTo op

Variablec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Variable

A named placeholder for a value declared by a Behavior or Step, bound to an actual value only once the corresponding execution occurs.
has super-classes
Cyber Entity c
is in domain of
boundTo op, boundToLiteral dp, variableName dp
is in range of
guardVariable op, hasInputVariable op, hasOutputVariable op, predictsVariable op

VersionedProductc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#VersionedProduct

Instances of stonework:VersionedProduct may include operating systems, applications, libraries, devices, or embedded components at a specific release. Versioning, vendor attribution, and edition details SHOULD be represented using explicit properties rather than encoded strings.
A specific versioned release or build of a Product, identified by a CPE name or equivalent product identifier. Represents the unit of software actually deployed and potentially affected by vulnerabilities.
has sub-classes
Malware Sample c
is in domain of
cpeUri dp, dependencyOf op, hasDependency op, implementsTechnique op, isVulnerableTo op, purl dp, supersedes op, version dp, versionOf op
is in range of
affected op, appliesTo op, dependencyOf op, fixedInProduct op, has installed product op, hasDependency op, hasVersion op, installation of op, supersedes op, targetsPlatform op
is disjoint with
Product c

Vulnerabilityc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Vulnerability

A flaw or weakness in software, hardware, firmware, or system architecture that can be exploited by a threat actor to compromise confidentiality, integrity, or availability.
has super-classes
Security Condition c
is in domain of
affected op, cveId dp, cvssBaseScore dp, cvssScore dp, cvssSeverity dp, cvssVector dp, dateAssigned dp, datePublic dp, dateUpdated dp, epssScore dp, exploitsWeakness op, fixedInProduct op, hasCvssMetric op, hasWeakness op, isKnownExploited dp, reportedIn op, supersededBy op, vulnerabilityId dp
is in range of
isVulnerableTo op, mitigatesVulnerability op, remediates op, supersededBy op, weaknessOf op

Vulnerability Assessmentc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#VulnerabilityAssessment

A structured evaluation of a specific vulnerability's applicability and risk in a particular product or deployment context.
has super-classes
Assessment c

Weaknessc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://cyberterrain.org/ns/stonework#Weakness

Instances of stonework:Weakness may represent base weaknesses, variant weaknesses, or compound weaknesses. CWE identifiers (e.g., "CWE‑79") SHOULD be modeled using explicit properties rather than encoded in the class IRI. Descriptions and extended details SHOULD be referenced via citations rather than reproduced verbatim.
A type of flaw, fault, or design condition in software, hardware, or system architecture that can enable vulnerabilities, reduce security assurance, or increase the likelihood of exploitable behavior.
has super-classes
Security Condition c
is in domain of
cweAbstractionLevel dp, cweId dp, weaknessOf op
is in range of
exploitsWeakness op, hasWeakness op, remediates op
